security_audit.summary: AI review found no malicious intent, prompt injection, hidden payloads, or credential exfiltration. The confirmed risk is that the runnable FastAPI example binds to all interfaces and accepts voice WebSocket clients without an auth gate. The remaining static alerts are documentation or sample-code false positives, including Markdown backticks, mock audio byte literals, placeholder credential paths, and commented provider API-key examples.

remediation.issue: Example server listens on all network interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default and document when external binding is appropriate behind TLS, authentication, and network controls.

remediation.issue: Voice WebSocket example accepts clients without access control.
remediation.suggestion: Add an authentication and origin-check example before websocket.accept(), plus basic rate limiting for incoming audio streams.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholders may be copied into unsafe configurations.
remediation.suggestion: State that provider keys and Google credential files must come from a secret manager or protected environment, never from committed config.

content.value_statement: Real-time voice apps need careful orchestration of audio, transcription, LLM responses, and speech synthesis. This skill provides architecture patterns, templates, and examples for responsive conversational voice engines.
actual_capabilities: Explains an async worker pipeline for audio input, transcription, agent response, synthesis, and audio output.
Provides Python examples for streaming conversations, Gemini agent responses, and interrupt handling.
Shows a multi-provider factory pattern for transcription, LLM, and TTS providers.
Documents common latency, audio feedback, interruption, and provider selection pitfalls.
Includes templates for base workers and provider factories that developers can adapt.
limitations: It is guidance and sample code, not a complete production service.
Provider implementations in the factory template are placeholders that raise NotImplementedError.
Deployment security, authentication, and data retention policies must be designed separately.
Live provider testing requires valid API credentials and network access.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Use the worker pipeline and examples to plan a responsive assistant with streaming speech input and output.

use_cases.title: Compare Voice Providers
use_cases.description: Review provider guidance before choosing transcription, LLM, and speech synthesis services for a project.

use_cases.title: Improve Conversation Interruptions
use_cases.description: Apply the interruption patterns to stop bot speech, update transcript history, and reduce awkward audio playback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Voice Engine
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple real-time voice assistant. Include the worker pipeline, queues, provider choices, and the first implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Select Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare transcription, LLM, and TTS providers for my voice app. Recommend options for latency, quality, and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interrupt Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add interruption handling to an existing voice bot. Explain the event flow, transcript updates, and audio playback timing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my voice engine architecture for latency, backpressure, provider failures, security controls, and realistic testing gaps.

output_examples.input: I need a voice bot that can stop speaking when the user interrupts.
output_examples.output: A recommended design with transcriber mute control, interruptible events, rate-limited audio output, and transcript updates after partial playback.

output_examples.input: Help me choose services for a multilingual customer support voice agent.
output_examples.output: A provider comparison that weighs streaming transcription, LLM quality, language support, TTS voice quality, latency, and expected operating cost.

output_examples.input: Review my voice pipeline before I build the first prototype.
output_examples.output: An implementation checklist covering worker queues, WebSocket flow, audio formats, provider configuration, interruption tests, and production security items.

best_practices: Start with the queue-based worker model before adding provider-specific integrations.
Keep API credentials in secure configuration and avoid committing provider keys.
Test interruption, audio muting, and latency with realistic audio streams.
anti_patterns: Connecting every provider before proving the core conversation loop.
Sending full synthesized audio buffers before the client can interrupt playback.
Treating sample credentials or placeholder configs as production-ready secret handling.

faq.question: Does this skill build a complete voice AI product?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, examples, and templates that need production hardening.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support multiple speech and LLM providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes factory patterns for transcription, LLM, and TTS provider selection.

faq.question: Can it help with interruption handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains interruptible events, rate-limited playback, and transcript updates after partial speech.

faq.question: Are API credentials included?
faq.answer: No. Provider keys and credential files are placeholders and must be supplied securely by the user.

faq.question: What should I add before production deployment?
faq.answer: Add authentication, TLS, origin checks, rate limits, monitoring, error handling, and privacy controls for audio data.
